subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 28-year-old woman with anorexia nervosa has been fasting for 5 days in the hospital. Her blood glucose is maintained at 60 mg/dL, and she has mild ketonemia. Lipolysis in adipose tissue releases fatty acids that are oxidized in her liver.
question: Which of the following products of fatty acid oxidation in this patient can serve directly as a substrate for gluconeogenesis?
explanation_correct: Odd-chain fatty acids are oxidized to acetyl-CoA plus one propionyl-CoA in the final cycle. Propionyl-CoA is carboxylated to methylmalonyl-CoA by biotin-dependent propionyl-CoA carboxylase and then converted by vitamin B12-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase to succinyl-CoA, which enters the TCA cycle and can be used for gluconeogenesis; this makes odd-chain fatty acids the only fatty acid carbon source of new glucose.

explanation_incorrect.B: Acetyl-CoA cannot be converted to glucose in humans because the pyruvate dehydrogenase reaction is irreversible and there is no glyoxylate cycle; it is used in the TCA cycle or for ketogenesis.
explanation_incorrect.C: beta-hydroxybutyrate is a ketone body that is oxidized to acetyl-CoA in extrahepatic tissues and cannot yield net glucose.
explanation_incorrect.D: Acetoacetate is also a ketone body and is converted to acetoacetyl-CoA and then acetyl-CoA, which is not gluconeogenic.
explanation_incorrect.E: Malonyl-CoA is the product of acetyl-CoA carboxylase and a substrate for fatty acid synthesis; it is not a gluconeogenic precursor.

educationalObjective: Propionyl-CoA from odd-chain fatty acids can enter the TCA cycle as succinyl-CoA and serve as a glucose precursor.
